 Judgment
This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of Nanjundaiah S/o Muddamallaiah, in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioners that on 04.03.2024 at about 3.00 a.m., the deceased Sri.
Nanjundiah was travelling on his motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-42-EF-1656 near Byranahalli bridge, Magadi Huliyurdurga main road, Byranahalli gate.

At that time, the driver of the car bearing registration No. KA-10-A-7731 (hereinafter referred to as the "offending vehicle") drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
3. Due to the impact of the collision, the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
The dead body was immediately shifted to the Government Hospital, Magadi, where post-mortem examination was conducted, and thereafter the body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners performed the last rites and incurred expenses of about Rs. 50,000/- towards transportation, funeral, and obsequies.
4. It is further submitted that the accident and resultant death of Sri. Nanjundiah occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending car.

At the time of the accident,
the deceased was aged about 47 years, working as a Water Operator at Seegekuppe Grama Panchayath and drawing a salary of Rs. 15,051/- per month.
In addition, he was supplying milk to the KMFC flower vendor and was also engaged in agricultural operations, thereby earning

about Rs.
25,000/- per month.

sentences.text: The petitioners contend that they were entirely dependent upon the income of the deceased.
Petitioner No. 1 is the wife of the deceased, Petitioner No. 2 is his son, and Petitioner No. 3 is his mother.
On account of his untimely death, they have suffered mental shock, agony, emotional trauma, and have lost the breadwinner as well as the moral support of the family.
Hence, the petitioners have sought compensation of Rs. 30,00,000/- with interest, jointly and severally from Respondent No. 1, the owner of the offending vehicle, and Respondent No. 2, the insurer.
6. In response to the petition, notice was duly served upon the respondents.
Respondent No. 1 and Respondent No. 2 appeared through their respective counsel and filed written statements.

7. Respondent No. 1, the registered owner of the offending vehicle, admitted that he is the R.C.
owner of the car bearing Reg. No. KA-10-A-7731 and further admitted that the said vehicle was duly insured with Respondent No. 2 under a valid and effective insurance policy as on the date of the accident.
However, he has specifically denied that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the said vehicle.
It is his assertion that the accident was in fact caused solely due to the negligence of the deceased himself and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. Respondent No. 2, the insurer of the offending vehicle, in its objection statement, admitted the existence of the insurance policy in respect of the said vehicle and its validity as on the date of the accident.
However, it is contended that its liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Respondent No. 2 further contended that the owner of the offending vehicle had not complied with the mandatory provisions under Section 134(c) and Section 158(6) of the M.V. Act.
9.
It is specifically denied that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car.

On the contrary, it is contended that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the deceased, who was riding his motorcycle without wearing a helmet, without holding a valid driving licence, and thus it amounted to a case of self- accident.

It is also pleaded that the driver of the offending vehicle is a necessary party to the proceedings and that he had no valid driving licence, permit, or fitness certificate at the time of the accident.
10. Respondent No.2 has not specifically disputed the age, avocation, or income of the deceased, nor the relationship between the deceased and the petitioners.
However, it has denied the claim of dependency and quantum of compensation as claimed.
On these grounds, Respondent No. 2 has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

11. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that Nanjundaiah S/o Late Muddamallaiah died in a Road Traffic Accident occurred on 04-03- 2024 at about 3.00 a.m. near Byranahalli bridge, Magadi - Bhagyamma vs Jagadeesha V on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54236448/
3 huliyurdurga road, Magadi, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing reg.No.KA- 10-A-7731?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
if so, what amount?
3. What order or award ?
12. In support of their claim, Petitioner No.1 is examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17.

On the other hand the Respondent No.1 is examined as RW-1 and got marked the copy of RC at Ex.R.1.
13.
Having heard the counsel for both sides and have perused the material on record.

14. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative. Issue No.2 : Partly In the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 15. ISSUE NO.1:- Petitioner No. 1, who is the wife of the deceased, has filed her affidavit under Order XVIII Rule 4 CPC in lieu of examination-in-chief and was examined as PW-1.

She has reiterated the facts stated in the petition, namely that on 04.03.2023 at about 3.00 a.m., her husband, the deceased Nanjundaiah, was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-42-EF-1656 near Byranahalli bridge, Magadi Huliyurdurga main road, Byranahalli gate, when the offending car,
driven in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed and dashed against his motorcycle,
causing him to sustain fatal injuries and die on the spot.
16.
In support of her testimony, PW-1 has produced contemporaneous police records.
Exhibit P-1 is the FIR registered on the basis of her first information statement(EX P2).
Exhibit P-4 is the spot mahazar, and Exhibit P-5 is the rough sketch prepared by the police, both of which corroborate the manner and place of the accident.
Exhibit P-6 is the IMV report, which shows the damage to the vehicles involved.
Exhibit P-3 is the charge sheet filed by the Investigating Officer, which squarely fixes the responsibility for the accident on the driver of the offending car.
17. It is contention of the respondents that the accident occurred solely due to negligence of the deceased and not on the part of the driver of the offending car.
18. During her cross-examination, PW-1 admitted that the accident occurred at about 3.00 a.m.

However, she categorically denied the suggestions that the accident occurred due to negligence of her husband, that he was riding the motorcycle in a sleepy condition, or that a false complaint had Bhagyamma vs Jagadeesha V on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54236448/
4 been lodged for the sake of claiming compensation.

sentences.text: Except for these suggestions, nothing material was elicited in her cross- examination to discredit her testimony.
19. On the other hand, the owner of the offending car was examined as RW-1.
He merely reiterated the plea taken in the written statement that the accident was a self-accident due to negligence of the deceased.
However, no credible evidence was adduced to substantiate such a plea.
No independent witnesses were examined.

More importantly, if indeed the accident was a self-accident as alleged,
the respondents ought to have examined the driver of the car, produced contrary investigation records, or taken appropriate legal steps to challenge the charge sheet filed by the police.
No such steps were taken.
Thus, the plea of the respondents remains a mere bald allegation unsupported by material evidence.
20. It is well settled that in motor accident claim proceedings, the petitioners are not required to establish negligence beyond reasonable doubt, as in a criminal trial.
The standard of proof is that of preponderance of probabilities.

In the present case, the oral testimony of PW-1, coupled with the contemporaneous police records such as FIR (Ex.P1),FIS (EX P2), spot mahazar (Ex.P4), sketch (Ex.P5), IMV report (Ex.P6), and charge sheet (Ex.P3), collectively establish, on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities, that the accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
Accordingly, I hold that the petitioners have successfully proved Issue No. 1.
The same is answered in the affirmative.
21. ISSUE NO.2:-
The petitioners have asserted that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased Sri. Nanjundiah.

Petitioner No. 1 is the wife, Petitioner No. 2 is the son, and Petitioner No.
3 is the mother of the deceased.
In order to substantiate their relationship, the petitioners have produced Aadhaar cards of themselves as well as of the deceased, which are marked as Ex.P14 to Ex.P17.

On perusal of these documents, it is evident that Petitioner No. 1 is the wife of the deceased,
Petitioner No. 2 is his son, and Petitioner No. 3 is his mother.
Accordingly, all the petitioners are to be treated as the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased, and are therefore entitled to claim compensation under the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.
22. As regards the age of the deceased, the Aadhaar card of the deceased produced at Ex.P17 records his date of birth as 01.01.1977.
Since the accident occurred on 04.03.2023, the deceased was 47 years of age at the time of his death.

Therefore, as per the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 46-50 years is '13', which is accordingly adopted in the present case.

Thus, it is held that the petitioners have successfully established that they are the dependents of the deceased and are entitled to compensation, which has to be computed by applying the multiplier of 13 to the loss of dependency,
along with amounts under conventional heads.

23 . It is the case of the petitioners that the deceased, aged 47 years at the time of the accident, was employed as a Water Operator at Seegkuppe Gram Panchayat and drawing a monthly salary of Rs.15,051/-.

Apart from his regular employment, it is further contended that the deceased was also engaged in agricultural activities and was supplying milk to the K.M.F.C. and to a flower vendor,
earning an additional income of about Rs. 25,000/- per month.

It is their contention that the family Bhagyamma vs Jagadeesha V on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54236448/
5 was financially and emotionally dependent upon his income, and due to his untimely death, they have lost the sole breadwinner and suffered immense hardship.
24.

25. On the other hand, the learned counsel for Respondent No. 2 (insurer) has vehemently argued that the petitioners have not examined the author of Ex.P10 to Ex.P13, and therefore these documents cannot be relied upon.

He has placed reliance upon the decision in MFA No.

On careful perusal, it is noticed that although the petitioners have produced Ex.P10 to Ex.P13 to show that the deceased was working as a Water Operator and earning Rs. 15,051/- per month and was supplying milk to the K.M.F.C, the author of the said documents has not been examined.

Hence,
as rightly contended by the learned counsel for Respondent No. 2, the evidentiary value of these documents becomes weak.

Furthermore, with respect to the alleged additional earnings of Rs.
25,000/- from agriculture, milk vending, and flower vending, no documentary proof or independent witness has been produced.

27. Though, there is some material to show that the deceased was employed as a Water Operator, in the absence of examination of the competent authority and corroborative evidence regarding his exact earnings.

In such circumstances, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority (KSLSA) for determining notional income in motor accident claims, since the accident occurred in the year 2024, the notional income is taken at Rs. 16,500/- per month.
28. As the deceased was aged about 46 years, future prospects of 25% is added on the income of the deceased as per Pranay Sethi case.
Then the income would be .20,625/- p.m.

As there are 3 dependents, 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and the annual income would come to (Rs.20,625 - 6,875/- =Rs.13,750) (Rs.13,750 X 12) Rs.1,65,000/- and applying 13 multiplier, Petitioners are awarded Rs.21,45,000/- towards loss of dependency.
29. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Others1, this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the Petitioners are entitled Rs.44,000/- each under the head of consortium as Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 has lost his father and Petitioner No.3 has lost her son.

The loss to the estate is the loss of savings by the deceased.
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 has lost his father and Petitioner No.3 has lost her son.
Hence, Rs.20,000/- towards loss to estate.

33. Liability
The Petitioners have lead cogent evidence and have proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the Respondent No.1 and 2 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
However, in view of the issuance policy, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioners with interest at 6% per annum.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

34. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioners are awarded compensation of .23,13,500/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
